context: Emit every role a spec actually needs, sourced from the read model the build already produces rather than recomputed in JavaScript, then replace every literal and add a gate so the class cannot come back. Role identity matters - the funded/community fixture is not interchangeable with the canonical one, so the contract must name roles, not just platforms.
description: PR #1545 derived three of the fixture identifiers the browser specs use and left the rest as literals, so the Chromium suite is still red with 8 failures. Every hardcoded id in the suite is stale against the current build: the datafusion, tuned-duckdb, community-funded-duckdb and aws long ids, plus three short ids. compare.spec.ts is the clearest case - LONG_DUCKDB was replaced with fixtureIds.detailId while LONG_DATAFUSION on the next line stayed a literal, with fixtureIds.datafusionId already present and unused in the emitted JSON. The emitted contract exposes 2 roles while the specs reference about 6, and its allResultIds and shortIdLength fields have no reader. writeFixtureIds also reimplements the pipeline's _build_short_ids in JavaScript and assumes its input set matches the pipeline's all_result_ids, which replaces one drift class with another rather than removing it. Nothing prevents the next spec from hardcoding an id again.

work_units.evidence: fixture-ids.json now carries one entry per role, keyed by run.id, which is authored in the source bundles and the generator's own VARIANTS rather than content-addressed. 11 roles emitted (duckdb, duckdbTuned, duckdbCommunity, duckdbSf01, datafusion, datafusionPartial, awsCloud, containerLocal, gcpServerless, polars, starSchema), each with long and short ids. The generator now throws when a generated bundle has no role, when two claim one role, or when a declared role is missing from the build, so adding or renaming a fixture breaks the generator loudly instead of drifting the specs silently. Filename prefix could not do this: three fixtures share tpch-duckdb-sf0.01- and funding-disclosure.spec.ts depends on the community one specifically.
work_units.summary: Enumerate every fixture role the specs reference and emit each one from the generator

work_units.evidence: writeFixtureIds reads the pipeline's own short_ids table out of the built results.duckdb via a one-line uv subprocess, and the JS sha256 reimplementation plus its createHash import are deleted. The previous revision recomputed _build_short_ids from a comment describing it, with nothing enforcing agreement and an unstated assumption that bundle filenames matched the pipeline's all_result_ids; that traded one drift class for another. Emitted short ids now match the read model by construction. The generator raises if the read model has no short_id for an emitted result.
work_units.summary: Source short ids from the built read model instead of recomputing the algorithm in JavaScript

work_units.evidence: All 14 remaining hardcoded ids replaced across 10 spec files: a6bb8a70 (datafusion, 3 sites), a5eff54e (tuned, 2), b92a4ffb (community/funded), e73da6ce (aws, 2), 0820b170 (sf0.1 short, 3), 0f0add9f (star-schema short, 2), 009ee9fd (tuned short, 2). Four of those were missed by the ladder's own greps - two DUCKDB_SF01_ID assignments, a TPCH_SF01_SHORT, and an object property shortId: '009ee9fd' - because 'const NAME =' does not match an object literal; found by a shape grep over all string literals, which is what w3 turns into a gate. result-detail-failures.spec.ts also needed the fixtureIds import added; tsc did not catch it because tsconfig does not cover e2e/, only the Playwright run did.
work_units.summary: Replace every remaining hardcoded long and short id in the specs

work_units.evidence: Added tests/unit/scripts/test_e2e_specs_have_no_hardcoded_ids.py: shape-based detectors over every e2e TypeScript source, excluding *-output/ capture artifacts and comments. Proven non-vacuous both ways - clean tree 15 passed; planting a long and a short literal in compare.spec.ts fails both detectors, restored after. The short-id detector is deliberately not quote-anchored because the literal that survived the first fix was interpolated into a template string. It rejects CSS colours, longer words, and dated audit filenames (a real false positive from pr246-final-evidence.spec.ts) by requiring at least one digit and one a-f letter; the accepted blind spot is an all-digit short id, about 2.3 percent of sha256 prefixes, documented in the module.
work_units.summary: Add a gate that fails when any spec hardcodes a content-addressed identifier

work_units.evidence: allResultIds and shortIdLength are gone. Both were emitted by the previous revision and read by nothing (grep over results-explorer/e2e returns no use outside support/fixtures.ts). The payload is now exactly two maps, ids and shortIds, keyed by role. shortIdLength in particular only existed as a byproduct of the JS algorithm reimplementation removed in w1.
work_units.summary: Drop allResultIds and shortIdLength or give them a reader

work_units.evidence: Ran the suite rather than assuming it: npx playwright test --project=chromium --workers=2 gives 119 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed in 2.5m, against the previous run's 8 failures on PR #1545 CI run 30933934042. This is a local observed run on installed node_modules and a real build, not an inference - the earlier PR body admitted Playwright could not be run and shipped a claim CI then disproved. It also caught a defect the ladder and tsc both missed: result-detail-failures.spec.ts used fixtureIds without importing it, and tsconfig does not cover e2e/. Also green: npm run typecheck exit 0, vitest 862 passed across 70 files, fixture determinism verifier OK. CI on the pushed branch remains the authority for the runner environment.
work_units.summary: Confirm the Chromium suite is green in CI rather than assumed green
